skill.name: binary-re-dynamic-analysis
skill.description: Guides approved dynamic analysis of binaries with QEMU, GDB, Frida, Docker, strace, and sandboxed runtime observation.
skill.summary: Run approved binary runtime analysis with tracing, debugging, hooks, and structured observation.
skill.author: 2389-research

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts were Markdown syntax or documentation examples, but the skill still presents real operational risk. It instructs analysts to execute unknown binaries, includes a privileged Docker setup command, loads a user debugger script, and uses temporary files for sensitive traces.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the --privileged Docker command or move it to a separate administrator-only setup guide with explicit host impact warnings.
Require a preflight checklist that records approval, sample hash, sandbox boundary, resource limits, and rollback plan before any execution.
Update Docker and nsjail examples to deny network access by default and document any approved exception separately.
Write memory dumps and trace logs to a private analysis directory with restrictive permissions, then delete them after evidence is archived.
Avoid sourcing home-directory debugger scripts by default, or require users to verify the exact file before loading it.

content.value_statement: Unknown binaries can hide behavior that static review misses. This skill guides approved runtime tracing, debugging, and observation in controlled environments.
actual_capabilities: Select QEMU, Docker, Frida, GDB, or on-device workflows for target architecture.
Prepare syscall tracing and debugger sessions for runtime behavior mapping.
Capture files, network attempts, memory observations, and process activity.
Identify anti-debugging checks such as ptrace, seccomp, timing, and /proc probes.
Record dynamic analysis findings in a structured investigation journal.
limitations: Requires explicit human approval before any binary execution.
Does not make unknown binaries safe to run outside a sandbox.
Frida requires native architecture execution or a target device.
Docker and QEMU tracing can miss behavior or lack ptrace support.

use_cases.title: Triage Suspicious Firmware Utilities
use_cases.description: Observe syscalls, file access, and network attempts from embedded Linux binaries before deeper analysis.

use_cases.title: Debug Cross-Architecture Samples
use_cases.description: Run ARM or MIPS binaries from a Linux or macOS workstation with QEMU or Docker.

use_cases.title: Validate Static Analysis Hypotheses
use_cases.description: Confirm suspected behaviors with breakpoints, hooks, and structured runtime evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Binary Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a safe dynamic analysis run for this binary. Ask for approval before execution, verify sandbox settings, and list expected observations.

prompt_templates.title: Map Runtime Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Given this binary type and architecture, choose a QEMU or Docker workflow, define tracing commands, and prepare an observation checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a Cross-Architecture Crash
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up a GDB workflow for this ARM binary under QEMU. Include breakpoints, memory checks, and recovery steps for missing libraries.

prompt_templates.title: Instrument Network Functions
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Frida or debugger plan to observe connect and send behavior. Include architecture constraints, fallback methods, and evidence logging.

output_examples.input: I need to run an ARM firmware helper and see whether it contacts the network.
output: The plan recommends QEMU syscall tracing with a network-disabled sandbox.
It adds an approval checkpoint before execution and names the observations to collect.
It records expected evidence for connection attempts, file reads, and exit status.

output_examples.input: The sample crashes under emulation before main.
output_examples.output: The analysis identifies likely missing libraries, suggests checking ABI and loader paths, and proposes a debugger session with resource limits.

output_examples.input: I found anti-debug strings and /proc references.
output_examples.output: The analysis highlights anti-debug checks, recommends QEMU tracing before GDB, and records which hypotheses need runtime confirmation.

best_practices: Confirm sandbox, network policy, and target ownership before executing any sample.
Use read-only mounts and disposable work directories for unknown binaries.
Record commands, approvals, observations, and confidence for every experiment.
anti_patterns: Running unknown binaries on the host because emulation is inconvenient.
Using privileged containers without a documented administrative need.
Treating one clean run as proof that the binary is harmless.

faq.question: Does this skill execute binaries automatically?
faq.answer: No. It requires human approval before execution and asks for sandbox checks first.

faq.question: Can it analyze malware?
faq.answer: It can support controlled malware analysis, but it does not replace an isolated lab.

faq.question: Which tools does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers QEMU, GDB, Frida, Docker, strace, nsjail, and related reverse engineering workflows.

faq.question: Does Frida work with QEMU user-mode?
faq.answer: No. The skill notes that Frida needs native architecture execution or a target device.

faq.question: How should network access be handled?
faq.answer: Disable network access by default unless the analyst approves a specific network test.

faq.question: Can results be reused in reports?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a journaling format for runtime observations, hypotheses, and evidence.
